speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you are suffering from fatigue, flank pain, and fever following recent antibiotic treatment for sinusitis. Have these symptoms started suddenly, and is the pain in your side worse when you tap on it?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is concerning; could you describe the nature of the flank pain—does it radiate to your groin, and have you noticed any changes in your urine color or frequency? Also, are you experiencing nausea or vomiting?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm is highly suggestive of Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (Churg-Strauss), but the negative culture rules out a standard bacterial kidney infection. Have you had a history of asthma or allergic rhinitis, and do you have any skin rashes or nerve pain (neuropathy)?

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (Churg-Strauss Syndrome)

The history of asthma/allergic rhinitis, the rash appearing with antibiotics (drug-induced eosinophilia), and the specific urine findings are classic for this vasculitis. The negative culture rules out a simple pyelonephritis. Do you have any history of asthma or allergic reactions to medications?
